rules.identity: entries are sole messages; surface/channel indexes contain references. Semantic key is metadata, not runtime ID.
skippedCategories: CV/cover-letter names, roles, employers, universities, bullets, skill values and document dates
sample input bodies, contacts, filenames, transaction references, amounts, progress and quota fixtures
empty text, decorative marks, OTP digit cells and password masks
nontext icons/vectors with no default visible label
rules.dynamicCopy: Typed arguments replace fixtures; fixed 6-digit OTP labels and 3-step journey labels are UI instructions. Policy values remain proposed.
rules.gender: Neutral professional Arabic; flag gendered fixture forms; never infer gender from names.
rules.source: figma-en requires exact exported English provenance; translated entries retain observed nodeIds. figma-recovery records normalized recovery-master text matches, including sample values for typed placeholders. Only spec-only entries may have empty nodeIds: authored, nonvisual, email, SMS, accessibility, validation or unmatched specification copy. Keep these entries valid without claiming Figma publication; recovery behavior remains the later T014 increment.
gates: A01-A16 apply; product direction is not implementation/release approval
PDF-only launch; Word unavailable, future A05 matrix in D04. OTP A14-A16; Phase 1 SMS reset/recovery codes, Phase 2 SMS-only sign-in off
Legal processing/payment evidence and remaining company inputs are required; UI gateway copy stays neutral
rules.transactional: Snapshot initiating UI locale; resend preserves it; ar-SA fallback. Sender-neutral SMS without links. Email uses approved first-party locale-preserving action URLs.
rules.lingui: Keep existing config, en-US source, zu-ZA pseudo, PO compilation and Crowdin. Verify proposed extraction under /tmp; application source/catalogs untouched.
rules.reuse: One key per shared meaning; four identical-English roles retain distinct Arabic contextual/grammatical forms. No semantic key is a runtime ID.

rules.countedNouns: Arabic counts use zero/one/two/few/many/other; English one/other. Ordinal page/index locators are not quantity counts.
